the expression of the GluR1, 2, 3 and 4 receptor subunits in NTS of the rat and the effects of hypertension on this expression.
the role of the nucleus of the tractus solitarius (NTS) in the development and maintenance of hypertension.
the role of the NTS in blood pressure regulation and the potential involvement of the glutamatergic system.

the increased GluR3 expression in SH may be a compensatory mechanism to increase the sensitivity of the NTS to glutamate in order to maintain blood pressure.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the expression of the GluR1, 2, 3, and 4 AMPA receptor subtypes is increased in the NTS of spontaneously hypertensive rats, and that the GluR2 subunit appears to be more abundant in neuronal somata compared to neuropil.
there are differences in AMPA receptors in SH, but these are not the same as those found in WKY.
the expression of GluR3 is up-regulated in the NTS of spontaneously hypertensive rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found that the spontaneously hypertensive rats have a higher expression of the GluR2 and GluR3 AMPA receptor subtypes in the nucleus of solitary tract.
the expression of AMPA receptors in the brain is different between the two strains, which may contribute to the development of hypertension.
there is a significant increase in AMPA receptor expression in the NTS of the spontaneously hypertensive rats, and this increase is associated with an increase in the expression of GluR3.
